title: Safety Corridor: Tactical launch sprint handoff
summary: Cross-functional tactical handoff to finalize launch safety corridor. Reviewed canary plan, SLO stretch criteria, kernel fallback checklist, and incident escalation hops. Identified three immediate blockers: telemetry gap for prefix cache hit-rate, missing canary ramp automation, and legal sign-off on new data retention policy. Agreed concrete owners and due dates for each blocker and scheduled a dry-run on 2027-08-06.
next_steps: Run end-to-end dry-run (canary + rollback) in staging on 2027-08-06
Priya to provide missing telemetry dashboard for prefix/KV cache by 2027-08-04
Devon to land canary ramp automation (feature flag + runbook) by 2027-08-05
Legal to confirm data retention exception by 2027-08-05
Schedule short exec readout after dry-run (2027-08-06 afternoon)
action_items: Priya Nair - Build prefix/KV cache hit-rate dashboard and add alert - due 2027-08-04
Devon Ortiz - Implement canary ramp automation + rollback hook in infra repo - due 2027-08-05
Samir Desai - Run performance smoke tests for quantized kernels and report regressions - due 2027-08-05
Maya Chen - Coordinate legal sign-off for 90-day retention exception and share note - due 2027-08-05
Ari Kaplan - Draft dry-run plan and circulation deck, book exec readout - due 2027-08-04
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~72 minutes | Attendees: Ari, Samir, Maya, Devon, Priya, Liam

Auto-summary (may be rough): finalize safety corridor for upcoming launch; agree owners for telemetry, canary automation, legal; schedule dry-run.

00:00 Ari Kaplan: okay, hi everyone, thanks for being on time. I want to keep this tight — 45 to 60 minutes ideally, but we've got 72 on the calendar so we can take the extra. The goal is one: get to a green dry-run scheduled, two: unblock the three things that could stop ship.

00:18 Samir Desai: yeah, thanks Ari. Quick recap from eng side — the kernel fallback tests flagged a couple of odd lat spikes last night, looks like quant path had a small regen on 1k step prompts, not full regression but noticeable.

00:32 Devon Ortiz: uh-huh, that's the quant-skew thing we saw; my initial read is it's likely an ordering of kernels, fallback to fp16 is causing a longer path for some seq lengths. I have a patch in review to reorder kernel selection at runtime.

00:46 Priya Nair: from SRE — the bigger risk for the safety corridor is visibility. We don't have a single dashboard showing prefix cache hit-rate plus per-model kv eviction counts; without that we can't reliably detect early cache thrash during canary ramp.

01:05 Maya Chen: and Legal flagged retention on the telemetry payload — the new diagnostic traces persist raw tokens for 90 days by default; they want an exception documented before prod.

01:20 Liam O'Connor: so the three blockers are telemetry visibility, canary automation, and retention sign-off — is that fair?

01:28 Ari Kaplan: yep, that's the list. Let's go deeper — Priya, can you outline exactly what telemetry is missing and why it's critical for the canary?

01:40 Priya Nair: sure. Right now we have token-level latency and host-level GPU metrics, and we have a prefix cache counter per node, but it's not bucketed by model and seq-length. So during a canary we'll get aggregate hits but won't see, for example, a model-specific drop in prefix cache that would silently inflate latency. Need a minimal dashboard: (1) prefix hit-rate by model, (2) kv eviction rate, (3) tail latency p95/p99 by model, all with 1m granularity. Also an alert if prefix hit-rate drops >20% from baseline for 5 minutes.

02:07 Samir Desai: that alert is reasonable. How long to build it?

02:12 Priya Nair: with a small query and a Grafana panel — two business days max, if I get the event schema access.

02:19 Ari Kaplan: okay, assign that to Priya — put due date for Thursday EOD. I'll add it to the action items.

02:27 Devon Ortiz: on canary automation — current ramp is manual: ops pushes 1%, 5%, 15% over a couple hours, with human verification in between. We need a flag-based ramp with automated rollback that can flip back at 5% failure signal. I sketched a runbook and a PR that wires the flag plus a probe-based rollback hook, but it needs infra approvals and end-to-end tests.

02:52 Maya Chen: is the rollback hook tolerant to transient SLO blips? We don't want to roll back because of a 1-minute anomaly.

02:59 Devon Ortiz: agreed — plan is to use a composite signal: error-rate >1.5x baseline OR p99 latency > 200ms increase sustained for 5 minutes AND prefix hit-rate drop > 15% — so two of three signals to avoid flapping.

03:25 Samir Desai: that composite sounds good. Dev, how quickly can you get the automation landed if we prioritize?

03:31 Devon Ortiz: if we prioritize, I can have the feature flag wiring and basic probe hooks in by Friday, 2027-08-05, but it needs a dry-run to validate.

03:39 Ari Kaplan: good. That matches the schedule. Next, kernel fallback — Samir mentioned perf spikes with quant path. Samir, what's the acceptable rollback decision there?

03:50 Samir Desai: from eng standpoint, if quantized kernel increases p99 by > 10% on a sustained basis for a model under canary, we should fallback to fp16 for that model. But we need test artifacts: perf comparison scripts and a small benchmark dataset hitting common seq patterns.

04:12 Priya Nair: can we reuse the existing perf harness? I can wire the harness into the canary lane to run checks every ramp step.

04:20 Samir Desai: yes, that'd be ideal. I'll write the benchmark set — five prompt families: short chatty, long context, code-gen, embeddings-ish, and structured output — should catch regressions.

04:36 Maya Chen: legal retention — quick note: Legal will accept a documented exception if the telemetry is token-truncated and access controls are enforced. They want a short note describing exactly what fields are retained and who has access. I can draft it with Legal if Priya gives the telemetry schema.

04:56 Priya Nair: I will paste the event schema to the doc by EOD tomorrow.

05:04 Ari Kaplan: excellent. Let's walk through the dry-run plan — scheduled for Saturday, 2027-08-06, morning window. We will run a staged canary up to 15% with automation, watch the composite signals, and execute rollback if triggered. Post-dry-run we'll do an exec readout same day.

05:25 Liam O'Connor: note: ops on-call availability — we'll need the primary on-call and a second person to handle manual interventions in case the automated hooks misfire. Can we get volunteer list?

05:36 Samir Desai: I'll be on-call that day. Priya can be second.

05:40 Priya Nair: yep, I can take second.

05:43 Devon Ortiz: I'll be available for infra touch.

05:46 Ari Kaplan: perfect. Triage chain noted in the runbook — include pager numbers.

06:00 [Speaker 7 - background] Someone: (muffled) sorry, joining late, ran into a calendar issue.

06:07 Ari Kaplan: no worries, quick recap: three blockers — telemetry dashboard, canary automation + rollback, legal retention sign-off. Dry-run scheduled 2027-08-06 morning. Owners: Priya, Devon, Samir, Maya for legal coordination.

06:28 Samir Desai: on benchmarks — I want to flag that quant regressions sometimes only show up at scale; local tests may be fine. Can we run a small-scale ramp in staging that mimics real concurrency?

06:41 Devon Ortiz: yes, staging cluster can emulate ~20% of prod concurrency using synthetic traffic; I'll prepare a traffic script. Need to coordinate with capacity team to carve out nodes.

06:52 Priya Nair: telemetry wise, can we get 1-minute granularity for the dashboard? Some of the cache churn happens quickly.

06:58 Ari Kaplan: yes, 1-minute as Priya requested.

07:05 Maya Chen: legal — I'll loop in Carla from Legal after the call. Carla wants the exact retention TTLs and redaction policy in writing.

07:15 Ari Kaplan: okay let's capture action items — we listed them earlier in the doc, but let's say them out loud for the transcript. Priya will build the prefix/KV dashboard by Thursday EOD; Devon lands the canary automation by Friday; Samir completes perf benchmarks and runs smoke tests by Friday; Maya coordinates legal sign-off by Friday; Ari prepares dry-run and exec deck by Thursday. Everyone confirm?

07:44 All: yes / confirmed / sounds good.

07:50 [small cross talk about calendar times]

08:05 Ari Kaplan: One more item — observation retention in logs for 90 days might be too long for some customers; for this internal run it's ok with the exception but we should add a config toggle to reduce retention in prod if requested. Low priority but note it.

08:25 Devon Ortiz: yep I'll add a feature flag for retention TTLs in the telemetry pipeline. Non-blocking for the dry-run.

08:33 Priya Nair: also, we should record the dry-run and collect a postmortem checklist template in case we hit an incident — quick blameless postmortem with prepopulated fields.

08:47 Ari Kaplan: good point. Liam, can your team templated postmortem?

08:52 Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll prep a short template and attach it to the runbook.

09:00 Maya Chen: timeline check — can we set an interim sync on Thursday morning to make sure dashboards and docs are in place?

09:07 Ari Kaplan: Thursday 14:00 UTC works for me.

09:12 Samir Desai: fine.

09:15 Devon Ortiz: works.

09:18 Priya Nair: I'll be there.

09:20 Ari Kaplan: excellent. Anything else?

09:25 Samir Desai: question — if the canary automation triggers rollback, how do we handle partially degraded models vs global rollback? Are we doing per-model rollbacks?

09:36 Devon Ortiz: plan is per-model rollback where possible — the runtime supports model-scoped routing. Only if multiple models fail do we consider a broader rollback. That reduces blast radius.

09:50 Maya Chen: and the canary ramp percentages are 1% -> 5% -> 15% over 2 hours with 20 minute observation windows?

09:56 Devon Ortiz: yes, that's the current plan. Could shorten observation to 10 minutes if metrics are stable but let's start conservative.

10:10 Ari Kaplan: ok, last call — everyone has action items in the notes. I'll follow up with calendar invites for Thursday sync and Saturday dry-run. Thanks all, over and out.

(End of recording)
